topics.flagship-ru-ua: Zelenskyy called President Trump's description of Putin as "my friend" "strange" because Putin is "an aggressor and a killer" (8 outlets). Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte, meeting at Mar-a-Lago, urged Russia to avoid actions that would expand the war, and Trump called on Putin to halt aggression even as Washington reportedly postpones a major overhaul of its European military footprint. Italian PM Meloni warned Kyiv the war "cannot spread to the Mediterranean" after Zelensky confirmed Ukrainian drones destroyed the Russian vessel Merkury at a Benghazi port. Zelenskyy also reportedly warned of an imminent major Russian strike on the power grid, and EU leaders failed to break a $1.7 trillion budget deadlock.
topics.flagship-ir-il: Houthi media say a Saudi strike killed 11 civilians in Yemen's Taiz, with the Houthi-coalition fighting deepening Yemen's humanitarian crisis (7 outlets). Trump reportedly said the US could hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site if strikes resume, while Iran's foreign minister says Qatari and Pakistani mediation continues. Separately, Iran is reportedly denying responsibility for an attack in Kuwait that killed Italians. In Gaza, Israeli strikes reportedly killed senior education official Khaled Abu Nada and seven others, and a Hamas official says the Hamas chief's son survived an Israeli airstrike.
topics.T15: Severe storms hit both US coasts over Thanksgiving, disrupting travel and leaving hundreds of thousands without power (9 outlets). Single-outlet reports describe king tides and high surf damaging the California coast, flooding risk and evacuation orders on Vancouver Island, and river flooding displacing families in Volusia County, Florida. A tsunami-alert civil security exercise is planned on the French Riviera.
topics.T01: Coverage is sparse. Britain has reportedly contacted 100,000 veterans about a possible wartime call-up, amid reports of growing civilian preparedness across Europe (2 outlets). South Korea let one of seven rescued North Korean fishermen resettle in the South and returned the other six.
topics.T02: The UN warned that famine is expected to rise because of global conflict and El Niño, which drives three of four newly identified hotspots, mainly in Africa (8 outlets). Other reports cover child stunting, a meningitis surge and malnutrition in Gaza, relief deliveries in Myanmar, and the effects of US aid cuts on American farmers. One outlet reports a Taliban directive to replace Afghan women's names with terms such as "granny" or "goat".
topics.T03: No chemical or biological attack is reported. The stories center on an OPCW meeting in The Hague, where Syria outlined efforts to address the Assad-era chemical weapons legacy and Nepal reaffirmed its Chemical Weapons Convention commitment. Sudan failed to win an OPCW Executive Council seat amid allegations that its army used chemical weapons, and a separate report concerns burial sites of Japan's wartime chemical weapons.
topics.T04: A Kenyan High Court ruled that the government violated the constitution by allowing a US-backed Ebola quarantine facility to be built without public participation (6 outlets). Nigerian reports say Borno accounts for nearly 90% of suspected cholera cases and that Gombe released outbreak-response funds. South Korea is introducing random quarantine inspections of arriving aircraft and ships, and Gaza meningitis cases are reportedly rising.
topics.T05: Guinea-Bissau's military leaders delayed the return to civilian rule until 2028, a year after their coup and despite promising a 12-month transition (2 outlets). Serbia arrested Informer TV owner Dragan Vucicevic, prompting questions over whether it is accountability or a political power struggle. North Korea reportedly shut a Swiss diplomatic office in Pyongyang and expelled its head.
topics.T06: A single outlet reports France has fallen into technical recession, with GDP down 0.2% in Q3, and that Macron faces mass protests over fuel prices. It reports one protester killed, over 100 injured, and about 244,000 participants in around 2,000 protests, including calls for Macron to resign. The account mixes terms such as "far-left riots" and "yellow vests" and is unverified.
topics.T07: No nuclear detonation or attack is reported. North Korea's Kim Jong Un visited nuclear-material production facilities and vowed to build more nuclear weapons after ignoring a Trump overture (2 outlets). An opinion piece ahead of the UN nuclear ban treaty conference urges a choice between abolition and catastrophe.
topics.T08: Armed men killed 13 National Guard soldiers and wounded 20 in an attack on an outpost in western Niger, the defense ministry said (4 outlets). Gujarat's ATS arrested an Assam youth over an alleged JeM-linked plot, and German police arrested three teenagers from a far-right terror group. Other reports cover an attack on Syrian Internal Security Forces in Hasakah, bandit violence in Zamfara, and a Yemeni ambassador's warning about the Houthis.
topics.T10: Coverage is a scattering of unrelated items. India is reportedly set to deploy its fifth S-400 system near Pakistan, and one outlet reports China is developing a covert submarine. Others cover Chinese drones spreading among Southeast Asian militaries, Serbia's push for higher defense spending, and Trump saying NATO is becoming "self-sufficient" after talks with Rutte.
topics.T11: India and Malaysia launched the sixth Harimau Shakti exercise in Ipoh, focused on sub-conventional warfare (5 outlets). India and Nepal began the 20th Suryakiran exercise, running to December 8 with 334 personnel from each side, focused on counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism in difficult terrain.
topics.T12: A "cyber incident" knocked almost all UK pensions and benefits systems offline, and its cause is not publicly known (3 outlets). Reports also describe a wave of breaches of US government systems, including the Air Force's Cloud One platform (reported), Treasury, the FBI, and a CIA/ODNI open-source system. SAP confirmed a security incident, FIFA confirmed a criminal cyberattack, and attackers are exploiting two critical Drupal flaws.
topics.T13: UK net migration fell to 77,000 in the year to June 2026, the lowest since 1997 excluding the pandemic (5 outlets). Fourteen migrants died and about 90 were rescued from a boat adrift near the Canary Islands, and the islands' leader said they "cannot take it any longer" after a reported record 2,000 arrivals in one day. Other items are commentary on UK and US migration policy.
topics.T14: Coverage is thin: one outlet reports that around half a dozen Trump Cabinet members and senior officials have moved to secure military housing in the Washington area because of domestic political violence and threats from foreign adversaries, particularly Iran. No specific embassy threats are reported.
topics.T16: Spain holds a snap general election on November 29 that could end PM Pedro Sánchez's eight years in power, with coverage on a possible PP-Vox government and on housing as an issue (several outlets). In New Zealand, election results leave Conservative PM Luxon facing tricky coalition talks with a centrist kingmaker. Germany's BSW is reportedly positioned as a kingmaker, and a court in Andhra Pradesh ruled on an election-agent dispute.

bluf: Houthi media say a Saudi strike killed 11 civilians in Yemen's Taiz (7 outlets), as fighting between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed coalition deepens Yemen's humanitarian crisis. Armed men killed 13 National Guard soldiers and wounded 20 in an attack on an outpost in western Niger, according to the defense ministry. The UN warns that famine is expected to rise because of conflict and El Niño, which drives three of four newly identified hotspots, mainly in Africa. Zelenskyy called Trump's description of Putin as a "friend" "strange", and Trump and NATO's Rutte urged Russia to avoid actions that would expand the war. Severe storms disrupted Thanksgiving travel on both US coasts and left hundreds of thousands without power. Not covered above, a "cyber incident" of unknown cause knocked almost all UK pensions and benefits systems offline (3 outlets), amid reports of breaches across US government systems. Also notable, Italian PM Meloni warned Kyiv the war "cannot spread to the Mediterranean" after Zelensky confirmed Ukrainian drones destroyed the Russian vessel Merkury at a port in Benghazi, Libya.
